chunks: From him, raising it from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), said:
I said to him, 'The meat is dried, salt is sprinkled upon it, and it is dried in the shade.' So he said, 'There is no problem with eating it because the salt has changed it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat dried meat that has been salted and dried in the shade according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the permissibility of dried meat (jerk) relies on the transformative effect of salt, which preserves the meat and alters its state sufficiently to prevent spoilage. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of *istihlak* (transformation), where a minor change in substance or preservation method renders a previously perishable item safe, emphasizing practical food preservation techniques of the era.

en.hubeali:
From him, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The meat (which is) dried and the salt is sprinkled upon it, and dried in the shade’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with eating it because the salt has changed it’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
if meat can be dried up by salting and leaving in the shade. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful to eat it because salt has changed it.’”
